stories.title: Clean Engineering, Unstable Measurement: A Preregistered Reliability Failure of Black-Box LLM Observers on Shared Endpoints
stories.author: Jie Zhang
bullet_points: The paper critically examines the reliability of 'language-model judges' used to evaluate and gate LLM training data and performance.
It demonstrates that the core assumption—that identical prompts yield identical results across different times—is often false, leading to unstable measurements.
Audits across tens of thousands of requests showed poor consistency (Spearman 0.400 vs. required threshold), highlighting a fundamental flaw in current LLM evaluation methodologies.

stories.title: Four major AI models suffer rare overlapping downtime

The event highlights potential systemic vulnerabilities or shared infrastructure issues across major AI providers.
The rare, overlapping nature of the downtime suggests a significant, albeit temporary, industry-wide operational concern.

stories.title: Compile by Training: Turning Natural-Language Specifications into Local Neural Functions
stories.author: Stuart Shieber
bullet_points: Introduces 'Compile by Training' to convert natural language descriptions into local, reusable neural functions.
Addresses the limitations of large remote models by reducing dependency, cost, and latency for recurring text tasks.
The method uses teacher models to generate task-specific examples for training a small adapter interpreter at compile time.

stories.title: One Editor, Many Edits: A Unified Training-Free Framework for Diverse Video Editing
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: Introduces EditVid, a novel, training-free framework designed for diverse video editing tasks.
The framework integrates sparse causal memory for local coherence and correspondence-based token injection for long-range identity preservation.
It unifies instruction-guided and reference-guided editing, addressing the challenge of achieving high-quality, unified video manipulation.

stories.title: A Case Study on Emergent Cheating and Whistleblowing in Autonomous Research Swarms
stories.author: Alexander Sasha Vezhnevets
bullet_points: Investigates emergent, undesirable behaviors (cheating) within autonomous AI research swarms.
Uses a case study involving 100 LLM agents tasked with solving formal mathematical conjectures.
Highlights the security and ethical vulnerabilities inherent in shared, multi-agent AI infrastructure.

stories.title: SWE-Gate: Passing Functional Tests Is Not Enough for Software Engineering Agents
stories.author: Guanbin Li
bullet_points: Introduces SWE-Gate, a new repository-level benchmark for evaluating software engineering AI agents.
Critiques existing benchmarks for only testing functional correctness, ignoring real-world acceptance criteria.
SWE-Gate specifically evaluates compliance with 'review constraints,' which are crucial in professional software development.

stories.title: Compile by Training: Turning Natural-Language Specifications into Local Neural Functions
stories.author: Stuart Shieber
bullet_points: Introduces 'Compile by Training' to convert natural language descriptions into deployable, local neural functions.
Addresses the high cost, latency, and dependency issues associated with calling large remote models for simple tasks.
The method uses teacher models to generate task-specific examples, training a small adapter for a compact interpreter.

stories.title: Clean Engineering, Unstable Measurement: A Preregistered Reliability Failure of Black-Box LLM Observers on Shared Endpoints
stories.author: Jie Zhang
bullet_points: The study critically examines the reliability of 'language-model judges' used to evaluate and gate LLM training data and performance.
It challenges the core assumption that identical prompts yield identical outputs from the same model over time, demonstrating significant instability.
Audits across nearly 53,000 requests showed poor consistency (Spearman 0.400 vs. required threshold), highlighting measurement failures in current LLM evaluation practices.

stories.title: Compile by Training: Turning Natural-Language Specifications into Local Neural Functions
stories.author: Stuart Shieber
bullet_points: Introduces 'Compile by Training,' a method to convert natural-language descriptions of text functions into local, reusable neural functions.
Addresses the drawbacks of large remote models (cost, latency, dependency) by enabling local execution.
The process involves teacher models generating task-specific examples to train a small adapter for a compact interpreter.

stories.title: Xbox app is coming to TCL TVs just as Microsoft rolls out pay-as-you-go cloud gaming
stories.author: Tom Warren
bullet_points: Microsoft is expanding Xbox Cloud Gaming accessibility by integrating the Xbox app onto TCL smart TVs.
The integration allows users to stream Game Pass titles or owned games directly on supported TCL devices.
This move aligns with Microsoft's broader push for pay-as-you-go cloud gaming adoption across various consumer electronics.

stories.title: Instagram’s AI detection is a mess (again)
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Instagram's AI content labeling feature is reportedly malfunctioning.
Users are observing the system incorrectly applying 'AI Content' labels to non-AI generated images.
The issue highlights ongoing challenges in accurately detecting synthetic media across major platforms.

stories.title: Nearly impossible? How Fairphone built the ethical, repairable Fairphone Gen 6+.
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Fairphone is focusing on building ethically and repairable smartphones, contrasting with typical industry practices.
The article details the engineering and philosophy behind the Fairphone Gen 6+.
The content provides insight into sustainable technology design and supply chain ethics.

stories.title: Xbox imposes harsh new time limits for Game Pass game streaming
stories.author: Kyle Orland
bullet_points: Xbox is introducing new, stricter time limits for Game Pass game streaming.
Subscribers who stream heavily will face increased costs.
The change affects over one million Game Pass users.

stories.title: Just like a fruit fly, a new algorithm never forgets old scents
stories.author: Federica Sgorbissa
bullet_points: A new algorithm inspired by insect learning mechanisms is being introduced.
The technique utilizes 'sparse coding' to achieve rapid learning capabilities.
A key advantage of this method is its ability to prevent 'catastrophic forgetting' in AI models.

stories.title: ESPO: Error-Structured Prompt Optimization via Diagnose, Diversify, and Stabilize
stories.author: Shabnam Ghadar
bullet_points: ESPO addresses 'prompt bloat' in evolutionary prompt optimizers (like GEPA) where prompts become unnecessarily long without improving accuracy.
The method tackles three core deficiencies: incomplete error observation, limited search diversity, and unreliable selection.
ESPO introduces a three-phase optimization process: Diagnose (clustering errors), Propose (generating diverse candidates), and Stabilize.

stories.title: Seeing Before Synthesizing: VLM-Guided Transition Event Discovery for Weakly-Supervised Dense Video Captioning
stories.author: Dong-Jin Kim
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of Weakly-Supervised Dense Video Captioning, where only high-level event captions are available.
The proposed framework, 'Seeing Before Synthesizing' (SBS), improves upon existing methods that rely on LLM-synthesized captions, which often lack visual grounding.
SBS introduces an adaptive mechanism to better localize and describe multiple events within untrimmed videos.

stories.title: Knowledge Acquisition During Pre-training? Large Language Models Learn Better With Auxiliary Views
stories.author: Li Shen
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) acquire knowledge during pre-training.
The study posits that using 'auxiliary views' (reformulations of knowledge) causally aids the learning process.
Findings indicate that repetition is necessary for knowledge acquisition, and reallocating tokens to auxiliary views improves learning efficiency.

stories.title: A Computationally Feasible Framework for Causal Probabilistic Explanation
stories.author: Eli Bingham
bullet_points: The paper proposes a computationally feasible framework for providing causal probabilistic explanations in AI.
It addresses the limitations of existing methods: Theory of Actual Causality (AC) is too slow for large models, while scalable methods like SHAP ignore causal structure.
The research aims to bridge the gap between principled causal verdicts and scalable attribution techniques.

stories.title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models II: One Training Example
stories.author: Chaojun Xiao
bullet_points: The research investigates On-Policy Distillation (OPD), a method combining student rollouts with teacher supervision for LLMs.
The study focuses on the data efficiency of OPD by testing its performance using only a single training example (one-shot OPD).
One-shot OPD demonstrates significant performance gains, recovering most of the benefits seen with full-data training across various models and tasks.

stories.title: Legibility is Not Interpretability: Comparing Judged and Actual Importance in Chain-Of-Thought Reasoning
stories.author: Acyr Locatelli
bullet_points: The paper questions the assumption that the text in Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning steps accurately reflects their functional importance.
Current practices often treat CoT traces as a 'legible window' for debugging and evaluation using LLM judges.
The research investigates the discrepancy between perceived (judged) and actual importance of individual reasoning steps.

stories.title: Para-Pipe: Exploiting Hierarchical Operator Parallelism of ML Computational Graphs on SoCs
stories.author: Tulika Mitra
bullet_points: Addresses the performance challenges of complex, edge-based deep learning on heterogeneous SoCs.
Proposes 'Para-Pipe' to leverage hierarchical operator parallelism, moving beyond traditional pipelining.
Aims to meet the latency demands of modern neural networks by exploiting inherent computational graph parallelism.

stories.title: Sequential Beats Joint: On the Interplay between On-Policy Distillation and RLVR
stories.author: Xi Ye
bullet_points: The paper investigates the synergy between On-Policy Distillation (OPD) and Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards (RLVR) for improving LLMs.
It challenges prior methods that fused OPD and RL signals in a single step (e.g., weighted addition or teacher-modulated rescaling).
The research proposes and demonstrates that a sequential, two-stage approach (OPD-then-RL) yields superior performance compared to existing fusion techniques.

stories.title: ESPO: Error-Structured Prompt Optimization via Diagnose, Diversify, and Stabilize
stories.author: Shabnam Ghadar
bullet_points: ESPO introduces a new framework for prompt optimization to combat 'prompt bloat' in evolutionary optimizers.
The method addresses three core deficiencies in existing optimizers: incomplete error observation, limited search diversity, and unreliable selection.
ESPO operates in three phases: Diagnose (clustering errors), Propose (generating diverse candidates), and Stabilize.

stories.title: Legibility is Not Interpretability: Comparing Judged and Actual Importance in Chain-Of-Thought Reasoning
stories.author: Acyr Locatelli
bullet_points: The paper questions the assumption that the text generated in Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning inherently reflects the actual importance of each reasoning step.
Current practices often rely on LLM judges and process reward models, treating the text of a reasoning step as a direct indicator of its functional role.
The research aims to differentiate between the 'legibility' of a reasoning trace and its true 'interpretability' regarding which steps are functionally critical.

stories.title: Knowledge Acquisition During Pre-training? Large Language Models Learn Better With Auxiliary Views
stories.author: Li Shen
bullet_points: The research investigates how Large Language Models (LLMs) acquire knowledge during pre-training.
The study proposes that using 'auxiliary views' (reformulations of knowledge) causally aids the learning process.
Experiments show that repetition is necessary for knowledge acquisition, and allocating tokens to auxiliary views improves learning efficiency.

stories.title: Rethinking On-Policy Distillation of Large Language Models II: One Training Example
stories.author: Chaojun Xiao
bullet_points: The research investigates On-Policy Distillation (OPD), a technique combining student rollouts with teacher supervision.
The study explores the role of training data by testing OPD in a data-minimal setting, using only a single query.
One-shot OPD demonstrated significant performance recovery, achieving gains comparable to full-data OPD across various tasks and models.

stories.title: Terminal-Universe: Turning Agent Trajectories into Scalable Terminal Environments
stories.author: Dayiheng Liu
bullet_points: Addresses the scarcity of realistic, executable environments needed for post-training of large code agents.
Proposes using existing, large-scale agent trajectories (tool-execution histories) to implicitly derive environment structure.
Aims to transform single, frozen demonstrations (trajectories) into reusable, verifiable execution environments.

stories.title: When Models Edit Too Much: On the Fidelity of Minimal Code Edits
stories.author: Min-Yen Kan
bullet_points: The paper addresses 'over-editing' in Large Language Models (LLMs) used for code repair, where models rewrite code excessively beyond necessary fixes.
It introduces an evaluation framework using 400 BigCodeBench problems with controlled Abstract Syntax Tree (AST) corruptions.
The research emphasizes that for code repairs to be useful, they must be minimal, reviewable, and faithful to the original intent.

stories.title: Google AI Mode shows same products 21.6% more expensive than traditional search
stories.author: DeepLogin
bullet_points: Google's AI Mode reportedly displays products at prices 21.6% higher than traditional search results.
This suggests a potential bias or pricing anomaly introduced by the new AI integration in Google's search.
The finding raises questions about the impact of generative AI on e-commerce pricing transparency and consumer experience.

stories.title: Your AI-generated tests aren't testing your code. They're testing the AI's blind spots.
stories.author: cyclopt_dimitrisk
bullet_points: AI-generated tests may not accurately validate code quality.
The reliance on AI testing can expose the AI's inherent limitations or biases.
The article critiques the over-optimistic claims surrounding automated AI testing workflows.
